claims.text: Applying an alumina-based refractory ceramic coating to rollers and guide plates will protect them from erosion by high-temperature liquid aluminum relative to uncoated metallic parts.
Unprotected metallic components such as carbon steel suffer severe corrosion in contact with molten aluminum.
The proposed coating is a dense, well-adhered alumina-based refractory ceramic layer.
The relevant service environment involves prolonged exposure to liquid aluminum above 660°C under mechanical stress.
An alumina layer can form a chemically stable barrier against molten aluminum.
The alumina barrier resists dissolution and erosion by liquid aluminum.
Alumina is chemically inert toward liquid aluminum under the stated operating conditions.
Alumina has low wettability with liquid aluminum.
The chemical inertness and low wettability of alumina minimize interfacial reactions and physical erosion.
Alumina's high melting point allows the coating to retain physical integrity at the stated operating temperature.
Alumina-coated parts will have significantly lower corrosion rates than uncoated metallic parts.
Alumina-coated parts will have longer service lives than uncoated metallic parts.
Protection depends on the alumina coating maintaining adhesion and structural integrity.
Thermal shock or mechanical impact could compromise coating performance.
